title: Geometry & Trigonometry
description: About 15% of SAT Math. Area and volume, lines and angles, similar and right triangles, trigonometric ratios, and circles — with the reference sheet in reach.
goals: Use the reference sheet for area and volume formulas instead of memorizing them
Use angle relationships and similar triangles
Use the Pythagorean theorem, special right triangles, and SOH-CAH-TOA
Work with arcs, sectors, radians, and the equation of a circle

scaffold.title: Triangles, trig and circles
scaffold.content: The SAT gives you a reference sheet with every area and volume formula and the special right triangles — use it. What it cannot give you is which relationship the figure is hinting at.
keyPoints: SOH-CAH-TOA: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent
Complementary angles: sin x° = cos(90 − x)°
Arc length = (angle/360) × 2πr; in radians, arc = r·θ
Circle (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²: complete the square to find the center and radius

examples.problem: A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. How long is the hypotenuse?
In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is 10 and one acute angle is 30°. How long is the side opposite that angle?
examples.solution: opposite = 10 · sin 30° = 10 · 1/2 = 5 (the short leg of a 30-60-90 triangle).

problems.problem: Two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°. What is the third?
hints: Angles of a triangle sum to 180°

problems.problem: A cylinder has radius 3 and height 4. What is its volume?
A circle has radius 8. What is the length of a 90° arc?
hints: A 90° arc is 1/4 of the circle

problems.problem: In a right triangle with legs 5 and 12, what is sin of the angle opposite the leg of length 5?
A circle has radius 7. What is its circumference?
x² + y² − 4x + 6y = 12 is a circle. What is its radius?
Two similar triangles have corresponding sides 4 and 6. A side of the smaller triangle is 10. How long is the matching side of the larger one?
